newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Confidence returning to Australia housing - industry.
newsitem.headline: Confidence returning to Australia housing - industry.

text.p: Australian building industry groups said on Wednesday April housing finance figures showed there was some confidence in real estate despite the patchiness of the economy.
But the industry also said it was still waiting for clear signs that confidence in the housing recovery was broad-based.
Figures released earlier on Wednesday showed finance commitments for owner-occupied housing in Australia rose 12.2 percent by volume to 43,595 dwellings in April.
"Today's figures indicate that in a generally sluggish economy there is some confidence in real estate," Real Estate Institute of Australia chief executive Philip Eliason said.

"Building approvals data suggest that much of the activity in the housing market is currently centred on units (apartments) and townhouses, with the housing sector yet to show clear signs that its recovery is broad-based," he said in a statement.

Eliason attributed the rise in housing loans to last year's three official interest rate cuts, while Master Builders Australia also said the latest interest rate reduction, on May 23, should help to further lift the number of home loans.

"(The figures) indicate that the impact of previous rate reductions are starting to flow through into higher housing demand," Master Builders national director economics and housing Wilhelm Harnisch said in a statement.
"This increase augurs well for higher levels of dwelling commencements in the September quarter this year," he said.
"The May 23 cut in interest rates should provide a further shot in the arm, boosting buyers' confidence and further increasing new home building activity."
Housing Industry Association Ltd managing director Ron Silberberg agreed, saying the current improvement was particularly noticeable at the middle and upper end of the market.
